name: Journaling and mood
summary: Writing an experience down, returning to a moment that mattered, and choosing what to share: a journal is useful when it preserves the personal meaning and control over the history.
lead:
In the morning a person makes a short check-in; in the evening they talk a long thought through. A month later they look for a photograph, or want to discuss several entries with a professional. These are different ways of using one journal, and reducing them to the mood of the day is hard.

We look first at the ways of making an entry and at coming back after a pause. Then at reading the archive and choosing material for a conversation. Privacy is part of that path: a person has to understand what is stored, what is passed on, and how to get access to their own history back.

audiences.title: Starting an entry when thoughts are hard to put into words
audiences.body: When a thought has not taken shape yet, a blank page can get in the way. It helps to have a choice between naming a feeling, a question that fits, and a free entry by voice or in text.

audiences.title: Making sense of your experience over time
audiences.body: A long history is what makes it possible to recall an event and how it felt at that moment. A person goes back to specific entries and, if they want, gathers them for a conversation with a professional.

audiences.title: Keeping the private and the shared apart
audiences.body: A shared journal supports a conversation with the people close to you, while a private one keeps a space with no observers. When the two formats are combined, it matters to choose deliberately who receives each entry.

sections.title: Finding the right way to make an entry
sections.intro: A short check-in, a long spoken entry and free text can complement each other.

observations.title: Keeping the different states of a single day
passages: A single rating for a day can hide the way it went: anxiety in the morning and a calm evening do not necessarily add up to a meaningful average. If an entry is made in the moment of feeling, it needs a time and a context of its own, not an obligation to characterize the whole day in advance.

Several check-ins make it possible to reconstruct the sequence of events later. A weekly overview is useful when you can get from it back to individual entries and see what exactly has been brought together. A good visualization helps read the history while keeping the differences within a day, instead of one final label.

A check-in can include a short note of circumstance: after a meeting, on the way somewhere, before bed. A note like that helps make sense of the sequence later. An overview should not turn events appearing together into a confident explanation of causes: what a person needs first is their own entries.

quotes.text: I've been really enjoying Bearable! It's easy to track symptoms, moods, and health patterns throughout the day, which is exactly what I was looking for. The app is well organized, customizable, and helps me spot trends I might otherwise miss.

This app is great for the most part - you can add up to 6 habits under the free version which is fine for the most part. I like that you can add a note for each completed habit and then see a page where all of the notes are. I also wish there was an option to track moods multiple times a day as someone who wants to track my mood swings throughout the day.

I love the concept of the bubble being multiple colors, i wish it was more like a specific emotion, even simple ones that you can put in it, as your overall day can't be assumed right then and there unless you wait til the end of the day, which i struggle to remember and identify my own emotions by then.

observations.title: Keeping the voice part of the journal
passages: Voice and video can be the main way of keeping a journal. In the experience below, both talking feelings through and coming back to the video recordings are valued. Replacing them with text alone changes not the presentation but the activity itself.

Another review describes the value of expressing thoughts freely before they are sorted out. For an entry like that, what matters is not losing what was said during a pause or during processing. A transcription can make searching easier, but keeping the original audio should remain a separate choice.

The terms of access to a favorite format also affect whether the journal continues. The author of the last review lost interest after access to video changed. So before a history accumulates, the terms for making a new entry, reading an old one and moving attachments have to be clear.

quotes.text: I loved the idea of talkbook (now called Heartspring). I have a hard time speaking with other people, so being able to journal my feelings and practice speech at the same time was super helpful. I loved that the video journaling was saved in app so I could reflect on it later on instead of taking up space on my phone.
I think too much. I get tangled in those thoughts, and then my whole life gets a little crazy. This is a perfect way to get my thoughts out of my head and untangle everything.

I got this app back in Dec 2024. I loved being able to make little video diary entries. But they updated to 'Heartspring' and now you have to pay to record. You can type in your entry. But I think that loses the charm of it. Kinda lame now.

placements.title: Keeping the voice part of the journal

observations.title: Asking a question that fits
passages: A good question helps open a topic that is hard to put into words on your own. The review below asks for variety and for comparing old answers with new ones. So repetition is useful when a person understands its purpose, rather than getting the same prompt round and round.

A familiar ritual can keep its value even when the wording has worn thin. Someone can go on valuing the start of the day with a journal and still ask for different questions. That is a reason to refresh the content while keeping the familiar way of writing.

Splitting the day into morning and evening suits some users and becomes a reason to come back in itself. The stage of the day is worth choosing flexibly, with a free entry left available. Other personal practices may call not for new general questions but for their own language and structure — that is what the ideas below develop.

quotes.text: I've been looking for a journaling app that has prompts but not the same prompt over and over again. I can only come up with so many things I'm grateful for lol. This has a lot of good prompts, preloaded with 200 and you can add more, and I do like the idea of getting to compare my old answers to my new ones.

This app has become an important part to the start of my day. It helps me to stay grounded and appreciative. There is so much going on with the outside world. I need ways to keep peace on the inside. I recommend this app to my clients. My only feedback is to get more varied prompts. It seems they repeat.

Overall, this is an awesome app, and I plan on getting it back into my regular schedule. I love how the journaling sections are separated by morning and evening, as well as the organization of the prompts! Also, I love the challenges and quotes provided.

art.alt: Illustration for the theme “Asking a question that fits”.

observations.title: Carrying on from today
passages: A character or a streak of check-ins can make starting more pleasant: looking after a digital pet gives a concrete reason to open the journal. But that kind of support changes after a break. A counter reset to zero can overshadow the entries already made, especially when the gap was caused by illness.

Coming back is better built around continuation: show the path that was saved, let someone start from today’s state and, if they want, explain the pause. The game layer should stay a helper you can follow, with any extra events under control. A personal history does not have to depend on a flawless streak.

After a break it should be possible simply to open a new entry, leaving the earlier history where it is. An optional note about the pause helps the person themselves, but should not be a condition for continuing. An app’s gentle rhythm is set by transitions like these far more than by a friendly character on the first screen.

quotes.text: As someone who is bad at finding motivation for stuff, especially when it comes to gratitude, it's really motivating to make a digital bird happy.

Finch overall was a great way to get rid of bad habits and maintain a routine, although sometimes you can just forget about it. If that happens Finch does a great job asking you why you stopped using it and why you're using it again. Finch is very good at personalizing its 'daily tasks' based off of what you need.

This app shames you for missing one day! I had 107 days of journaling, got sick, missed 1 day and this app brought my streak down to day 0, as if all those other days of journaling were nothing!!! Don't like this app for that shaming feature!

sections.title: Going back to an entry and carrying a thought on
sections.intro: An archive becomes useful when a general overview leads through to a specific moment.

observations.title: Finding a moment by a detail you remember
passages: An archive answers specific questions: when an event happened, where a photograph is, what was said at the time. In the example below, search is what makes it possible to return to important moments years later.

Another way of reading is to see a whole period at once. A year-end video pulls many small entries into a sequence; the review below values the emotional experience of watching it, not the search for a single fact.

Both scenarios depend on the original material surviving. The voice of someone close cannot be replaced by the entry title left behind. So transfer and restore have to be tested together with the attachments, and unexpected memories and notifications kept under the person’s control.

quotes.text: I absolutely love this app! I've been using it daily for over four years and I have referred to it often with the search function to answer questions that come up. Because I attach photos to most entries, I can quickly come up with pictures of important events. The search function is invaluable.
I've used this app for three years now. I really love the idea of documenting each day. It's heart warming to see the video at the end of the year.

Daylio Randomly decided to delete all my voice recordings for the past 237 days. DO NOT DOWNLOAD THIS APP. I have been a loyal user since 2022 and I regret it. Personally memory with my grandma are gone I suffer from memory loss and this was the app I used to remember things and now that's gone.

observations.title: Carrying on a thought already started
passages: A follow-up question is useful when it notices what the entry says and helps name the thought more precisely. The positive review values a more specific continuation of the person’s own thought. Quality here is set by what changed in their own entry, not by how many lines the assistant produced.

Repeating general questions can produce the opposite experience. If a person has already explained what they are going through, one more “how are you feeling?” does not necessarily move the conversation on. What is needed is the option to end the exchange, return to your own text and keep the wording the person considers important.

Continuation also depends on the context being kept. In the example below, useful questions lost their point after the conversation was reset every week. Whether to keep or delete that history should be the user’s decision; an automatic reset must not be quietly dressed up as the promise of a long personal dialogue.

quotes.text: Wasn't sure what to think of the new Eva feature at first, but now I can't start my day without her feedback and questions. Forces me to be more detailed and specific, and feel like I can start my day with more actionable items. Love!
Instead of actually giving me any actionable advice or skills. The cbt ai agent just parrots useless questions back to me. Way worse then using Gemini even though this is supposed to be specialized.

I think it's good. I like how the Chatbot isn't like other apps, it actually remembers and analyzes everything you say and asks helpful questions. However, I hate how it restarts your progress every week… It's Sunday at midnight now, everything I said to the bot has been erased.

placements.title: Carrying on a thought already started
placements.body: Sometimes a thought is easier to carry on in conversation with a professional. The journal then needs a different function: to gather only the entries and questions the person themselves wants to discuss.

sections.title: Choosing where access ends
sections.intro: A private journal, a shared entry and a selection made for a conversation each need different visibility rules.

observations.title: Keeping privacy and a way back in
passages: A separate lock helps draw the line between access to the phone and reading the journal. Being able to write freely about feelings is tied here directly to a code or Face ID.

The choice of how you get in can matter too. But the convenience of unlocking and the way to regain access after losing the code are different questions. They are worth explaining before a single copy of a personal history has accumulated, and without requiring anyone to work through technical terms.

The cost of uncertainty shows in the case below: a person deleted the app hoping to restore the login, and lost the entries. A clear answer is needed next to recovery and deletion: which data will survive, where a copy exists, and what the chosen route cannot bring back.

quotes.text: its a good app to write down your feelings without anyone coming to snoop through it because it has a passcode or face ID for u to open the app. ive been using the app for two days now and i enjoy just blabbering about my day and how i feel. i have trouble expressing my emotions and i think this app helps.

this diary/journal app is probably the best one i've downloaded. all of the amazing features are free (not all but a good amount) no ads, and obviously the lock feature is something that i haven't seen before! i love how you can add a number pin if your forgetful like me, or add touch id.

This app is so useless! I forgot my pin ,I tried all pins I use but it won't open!…no forgot password option…I deleted the app maybe I'd be able to have access to my stuffs!!! Can't believe everything is gone!! I kept vital information about my life since 2021!! Only for it to be gone in a wink!!

art.alt: Illustration for the theme “Keeping privacy and a way back in”.

observations.title: Discussing what is chosen together
passages: A shared question gives a couple or a family a reason to talk about themselves outside their usual messaging. At a distance, being able to read an answer when there is time, and to go back to the previous exchange, is especially valuable. Here the product supports an exchange rather than merely storing two parallel notes.

It matters to tell a missing answer apart from an update that never arrived. The participants need visibility rules they can follow, a say in the topics, and access to what has already been written. Private entries have to stay separate from shared ones, so that continuing a family conversation does not mean opening the whole journal.

A shared question does not have to appear every day; it can come at a rhythm that suits the participants. Declining to answer, or answering late, needs no public verdict. When one participant leaves, it has to be clear which of the entries already written stay with each of them and what stops being shared.

quotes.text: I absolutely love this app! My husband and I currently live 3k miles apart, this app has allowed us to connect on a different level is a safe place! Best thing we have done for our marriage!
Really good for getting to know your family and friends better plus you get fun and exiting questions!

I bought this app for our anniversary. At first it was full of great questions and we would get about three questions a day and we loved filling them out. About two weeks later we only get one question per day and when I try to add a new list of questions or something. It just says 'try later'.

conclusion.title: Preserving the personal meaning of an entry
conclusion.body:
The first thing to choose is the main moment of use: a quick check-in on a state, talking a thought through, or returning to a memory. That moment needs a simple way in and a reliable way to continue after a pause. In the reviews gathered here, what people value is not the amount of analysis but being able to express what is theirs and to find that particular experience again later. So the safety of attachments, a recovery of access you can follow and control over what gets published matter more than new interpretations of the journal.

Prompts, a character and a shared conversation can strengthen the chosen scenario, but they do not have to be present together. Their usefulness is worth testing with one question: does it become easier for the person to start or continue their own entry. Automatic conclusions must not stand in for their words, and a selection chosen for someone else must not open the whole personal archive.
